-# Agent notes for widget
-
-## Widget is closed source. It is never published publicly.
-
-This is proprietary intellectual property. It is not open source, it has no licence file,
-and nothing in it may be published to a public registry under any circumstances.
-
-What that means in practice:
-
-- **Never publish to Maven Central.** `publish-maven.yml` deploys to one place, this
-  repository's own GitHub Packages namespace, and every artifact there is private. There is
-  no Central profile, no staging plugin and no signing key in this repository, and none may
-  be added. `pom.xml` says the same thing next to `<distributionManagement>`; treat both as
-  binding.
-- **Never publish the images to a public registry.** They go to `ghcr.io` under this
-  organisation and are internal.
-- **Never add a licence file or an open-source licence header** implying the code may be
-  redistributed.
-- **Never vendor this source into a repository that is public.** Survey is the consumer
-  and is itself not public; it shades widget into the enterprise and federal jars only,
-  and `scripts/verify-jar.sh` there fails the build if widget classes appear in the CLI
-  edition, which is the one that contains no private code.
-- If a task seems to need any of the above, it is the task that is wrong. Stop and ask.
-
-The open-source components in this estate are different and do publish to Maven Central:
-`notes-plugin-api`, `notes-cli`, `goatrodeo`, `coordinates`, `baharat` and `annatto`
-among them. Do not reason from how those repositories release to how this one should.
-
-## Tests shared with Survey
-
-[Survey](https://github.com/notes-co/survey) assembles the `notes` CLI and runs
-black-box integration tests against it that reuse **this repository's own test data**. It
-does not copy the data into its tree: `build-survey expectations` reads `test-fixtures.json`
-at the root of this repository, at the exact commit the shipped jar was built from (the
-commit recorded in `META-INF/git/<artifactId>.properties`), and exports what that file
-declares. Every unit test here and every Survey case derived from it share one ID:
-
-```
-widget/<qualified suite or class>#<test name>     code tests
-widget/<data path>[#<case id>]                    data-driven cases: the file's `id` field
-```
-
-Survey's `scripts/compare-test-ids.py` diffs those IDs against `tests/coverage/widget.tsv`
-and fails its CI on orphans, so keep these rules when you write or change tests:
-
-- **Put expectations in data, not in code.** A new fixture-driven expectation belongs in a
-  data file the unit test reads (see below for this repository's format); Survey can then
-  evaluate the same file through `notes` without a second copy.
-- **Every data file gets an `id`**, derived from its path exactly as the existing files do,
-  and the unit test that reads it must require it. Never hand-pick ids.
-- **Declare new data in `test-fixtures.json`**: an `expectations[]` entry (glob, format,
-  `idField`, how the fixture path derives) and a `fixtures[]` entry with a tier (0 committed
-  and small, 1 downloadable for a nightly run, 2 full corpora). Undeclared data is invisible
-  to Survey.
-- **Keep tier-0 fixtures small** (kilobytes to a few megabytes); anything large is a download
-  (`downloads[]` with a sha256) or LFS, at tier 1 or 2.
-- **Renaming a test or data file changes its ID.** That is allowed, but Survey's coverage
-  manifest will report an orphan; mention it in the PR so the manifest is regenerated.
-- **Keep the provenance plugin.** The jar must record its commit in
-  `META-INF/git/<artifactId>.properties`; without it Survey falls back to the release tag.
-
-### Here
-
-- `src/notes-plugin/src/test/resources/registry/` holds a Maven-layout repository
-  (generated by `make-maven-repo.py`, committed) and `expected-discovery.json`;
-  `RegistryDiscoverLocalSpec` serves it over HTTP and runs `WidgetBuilder.discover()`
-  against it. Survey runs `notes registry discover` against the same fixture and
-  expectation, so extend `expected-discovery.json` rather than asserting inline.
-- Anything the `notes registry` plugin exposes (`discover`, `run`, `cbom`, `status`, their
-  flags and output shapes) is what Survey can test; adapter internals and the live-registry
-  integration specs are not, and are marked so in Survey's coverage manifest.
-- The host is asked one thing only: `NotesContext.airgapped()`, which `RegistryCommand`
-  reads once at mount time. An edition that never uploads hides `registry run` and points at
-  `registry cbom`. Everything else the plugin works out for itself, because it can: how much
-  of a CBOM to build comes from whether Sassafras is on the classpath and whether
-  `report_cli` runs, not from the host naming its edition. An earlier draft did add an
-  edition accessor to the plugin API and it was dropped as duplicating what the plugin can
-  see — do not reintroduce it.
-- `SassafrasRunner` is reached through a `lazy val` in `LocalCbomProcessor` because a
-  distribution without static surveys has no Sassafras on the classpath at all, and the
-  class must not be linked.
